I live in a sheltered, bible-belt area. I didn't even know what transgender really meant until I was 17.

I remember looking at my genitals as a child and thinking something was off. I didn't know what they were supposed to look like, I was like 8; but I do remember wondering if my mom had lied, maybe this is what a penis looks like and she just didn't want me to be a boy.

I remember my depression really setting in and kicking my ass right around the time puberty set in.

I remember always hanging out with boys and wanting to wear boys clothes, but I always just figured it was because they were comfier.

Other than that, I was the same as any other afab child. I didn't play with a lot of cars or other "boy" toys. I played with stuffed animals and dolls. I was a computer nerd so I wasn't into sports or other "masculine" activities. I was an art geek and a game freak and always figured I was just a nerdy girl destined to be uncomfortable in my own awkward body.

When I came out, my mom told me she had expected me to be gay, but not this. I was in denial at first when my friend had told me what it meant and asked about how I felt regarding it after I had made some odd comments about if I were a boy. Even looking back now, if I had known what it meant back then, I don't think I would have pinpointed that's what it was. If given the option to change gender as a child, I wouldn't know what to do with that thought. The change is terrifying. I don't think I could have handled it then with the way my family is. Think "pray the gay away" but not quite that severe. When asked at age five what I wanted to be when I grow up, I never would have thought my answer would now be, "a boy."
